text.title: JPA / Hibernate Core Rules
text.summary: 12 testable rules grounding the Spring Data JPA + Hibernate methodology. Each rule pairs a binary check + sourced rationale. Rules 1-6 govern the runtime fetch / migration / test discipline; rules 7-12 govern entity mapping, repository shape and transaction ownership.

rule.statement: Every `@OneToMany`, `@ManyToMany`, and `@ManyToOne` association MUST set (or inherit) `FetchType.LAZY`. Eager loading MUST be opt-in per query via `JOIN FETCH` or `@EntityGraph`.
rule.rationale: EAGER fetch is global and unselective; combining two EAGER collections triggers `MultipleBagFetchException` or Cartesian explosions under load.

rule.statement: Entities MUST implement `equals` and `hashCode` over a stable business key (e.g. `naturalId`, externally-assigned UUID) — never over the generated DB id and never via Lombok `@Data`.
rule.rationale: DB id is null before insert and changes proxy semantics; Lombok `@Data` walks lazy collections and triggers infinite recursion plus DB loads.

rule.statement: Every diff to an entity (`@Column`, `@JoinColumn`, type change, rename) MUST land in the same PR as a paired Flyway migration. `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto` MUST be `validate` in `prod` profile.
rule.rationale: Without paired migrations, startup `SchemaManagementException` aborts the deploy or — worse — Hibernate auto-DDL silently mutates the prod schema.

rule.statement: Bulk update / delete repositories MUST annotate `@Modifying(clearAutomatically = true, flushAutomatically = true)`. Hand-written JPQL bulk ops MUST flush+clear the persistence context.
rule.rationale: Bulk JPQL bypasses the first-level cache; without `clearAutomatically`, subsequent `findById` calls return pre-update entities and silently corrupt logic.

rule.statement: Repository tests MUST use `@DataJpaTest` (slice) + Testcontainers. `@SpringBootTest` MUST NOT be used for pure repository tests. OSIV (`spring.jpa.open-in-view`) MUST be `false` in all profiles.
rule.rationale: `@SpringBootTest` boots the full context; slice tests run 5-10× faster, isolate schema issues from app logic, and force the LazyInitialization discipline at test time.

rule.statement: Controllers MUST return DTO projections, not JPA entities. Entity-to-DTO mapping MUST happen inside the transactional service layer, before the session closes.
rule.rationale: Returning entities to controllers crashes with `LazyInitializationException` once OSIV is disabled; DTO projections fix the contract permanently.

rule.statement: Every entity MUST carry created/updated timestamps via `@CreationTimestamp` + `@UpdateTimestamp` (Hibernate) or `@CreatedDate` + `@LastModifiedDate` (Spring Data JPA with `@EntityListeners(AuditingEntityListener.class)`). `createdAt` MUST be `updatable = false`.
rule.rationale: Auditing fields support compliance + debugging at near-zero cost; missing them forces post-hoc trigger work later. Manual timestamp management in service code is error-prone and misses bulk-update paths — Hibernate-managed timestamps are applied at the persistence layer regardless of which code path modifies the entity.

rule.statement: Every `@OneToMany` / `@ManyToMany` MUST carry an explicit Javadoc comment justifying its cascade, `orphanRemoval` and fetch choice. `CascadeType.ALL` is forbidden without a written reason; `FetchType.LAZY` is preserved as the default and `EAGER` requires justification.
rule.rationale: Unjustified `CascadeType.ALL` deletes data. `CascadeType.ALL` with `orphanRemoval = true` on a relation to an entity referenced elsewhere corrupts data: orphan removal deletes the child when it leaves the parent collection even if other entities still reference it. `EAGER` collections cause Cartesian explosions.

rule.statement: User-editable aggregates MUST declare `@Version` for optimistic locking. Inventory / balance writes where a lost update is unacceptable MUST use `LockModeType.PESSIMISTIC_WRITE` on the repository method, with the reason documented. The service MUST catch `OptimisticLockException` and surface a domain error.
rule.rationale: Without locking, two concurrent requests that each read then update the same row produce a lost update — the second write silently overwrites the first and neither party is told.

rule.statement: Services MUST consume a narrow repository interface listing only the operations actually used. Raw `JpaRepository<T, ID>` MUST NOT appear in service method signatures. `JpaSpecificationExecutor` is added only when dynamic filtering is required.
rule.rationale: Exposing the full CRUD surface tempts callers to bypass the aggregate boundary and to reach for operations such as `deleteAllInBatch()` that skip business rules; narrow interfaces are testable + auditable.

rule.statement: Read-only queries that do not need the full entity MUST project to a DTO (interface or class projection). Loading a full `@Entity` to populate a 3-field list view is forbidden.
rule.rationale: Entity hydration initialises every column, every Hibernate proxy and all auditing state — hundreds of bytes per row — for data that is never written. A projection generates a `SELECT` over only the required columns.

rule.statement: Service methods MUST be annotated `@Transactional(readOnly = true)` for query-only paths and `@Transactional` for writes. Repository methods MUST NOT be annotated `@Transactional` — the service owns the boundary.
rule.rationale: `readOnly = true` lets Hibernate skip dirty checking and the end-of-transaction flush on read paths. Service-owned boundaries let several repository calls join one atomic unit; repository-owned boundaries fragment them.

text.p: `lazy-by-default` and `datajpatest-for-repositories` together carry the eager-loading contract: eager loading is opt-in per query via `JOIN FETCH` / `@EntityGraph` inside the transactional boundary, and `spring.jpa.open-in-view` is `false` in every profile, so no lazy association is reachable outside it.
